info.title: Coco API
info.description:
Contract v1, served under `/api/v1`. **Deprecated** since 2026-10-05: every response
carries `Deprecation` (RFC 9745) and a `Link` to its v2 successor. It is removed after
seven days without uses (step 7.10).

Every successful JSON response is wrapped as `{ data, meta }`. Every error is
`{ error: { code, message, details } }`, where `details` lists the fields that failed.
Messages meant for the user are in Spanish.

Identifiers are integers (int64) and money travels as a decimal string.

field.description: The input field at fault, when there is one.

code.description: Stable, machine-readable kind: bad_request, unauthenticated, forbidden, not_found, conflict, duplicate, unprocessable, rate_limited, payload_too_large, unsupported_media_type, internal_error, unavailable…

message.description: Human-readable, in Spanish: the client may show it as is.

pending_approval.description: Whether an administrator must approve the account before it can sign in.

refresh_token.description: Native clients only (`X-Coco-Cliente: nativo`); the web gets an httpOnly cookie instead.

children.description: Present in the list (the tree), absent on a single category.

recurrente.description: Whether the concept is paid every so often.

estatico.description: Whether the cost center refuses reclassification from the transactions table.

dia_de_pago.description: Day of the month it is due.

mes_de_pago.description: Reference month of the cycle, 1–12. Only when the periodicity is not monthly.

presupuesto.description: Expected cost each time, as a decimal string.

pago_automatico.description: Whether the transaction is created on its own on the due day.

varios_pagos.description: Whether it is paid in several parts rather than settled at once.

palabras_clave.description: Words looked for in a receipt to recognise this concept.

recurrente.description:
── Recurrence ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Marks the concept as a payment that comes back. `dia_de_pago` is the day
of the month it is due; in months that do not reach that day, the last one
is meant.

estatico.description:
What hangs from a STATIC cost center is not reclassified from any
transactions screen. It is only read from the cost center; on a category
or a concept it does nothing.

mes_de_pago.description: The reference month of the cycle. Only when it is not monthly.

pago_automatico.description:
── Automatic payment ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
The concept does not wait for anyone to record it: when its payment day
comes, the transaction is created on its own and stops being pending.

For what is charged without anyone doing anything —a direct debit, a
subscription—. Only from the month it is turned on onwards: it never fills
past months.

It only means something on a recurring concept.

varios_pagos.description:
── Paid in several installments ────────────────────────────────────────
The concept is not settled with one payment: it is covered bit by bit.
Groceries take four trips, fuel six fill-ups, and none of those trips
closes the month.

When flagged, the concept stays in pending payments while what was paid is
less than what was expected, showing how much it has so far.

Three conditions, and the service checks them, not this: it has to be a
CONCEPT —the third level—, it has to be RECURRING, and it cannot also
carry «pago automático». All three are about how the row ends up after the
change, and here only the request is visible.

presupuesto.description:
── Budget ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
What it is expected to cost each time it comes due. When set, it RULES:
the month's forecast is this number and not the average of what it cost
before.

It is for the expenses whose amount is known —a rent with a contract, a
monthly fee— where averaging gives a worse figure than the datum. Empty,
it keeps averaging, which is right for what really varies.

Zero is a value, not a gap: it says «this costs nothing now». To clear it,
send `null`.

It only means something on a recurring concept.

palabras_clave.description:
── Keywords ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
What is searched for in a receipt's text to recognize this concept. They
only mean something on a concept: a cost center and a category do not
appear on any bill.

external_ref.description:
The idempotency key. The client generates it when capturing —a UUID— and
repeats it when it retries: the second time it gets what was already
created.

captured_at.description: When it was captured, ISO 8601 with a zone. Without it, now.

category_id.description:
The concept —or the category— the person chose in the phone's quick
form. The choice WINS over whatever the engine proposes; with this and
the amount, no text or merchant is needed.

It goes here and not in `POST /transactions` because the phone's queue
needs ONE idempotent endpoint —always 200, `repetido`, `resumen`— for all
its items. Sending the manual ones the other way would force reading the
unique index's 409 as a success and would split the queue in two.

cuentas_habilitadas.description: Whether this user keeps accounts at all.
